title: Safeguarded batching & cache advisor playbook and rollback tooling
creator: Mariko Sato
description: After a recent Optimize auto-tuning rollout that aimed to reduce per-token cost by increasing batch sizing and enabling longer-lived prefix/KV cache entries, we observed a 28% transient cost regression and increased tail latency for some workloads. This ticket captures the incident follow-ups: a postmortem summary, a set of mitigations, a codified playbook for safe config apply and rollback, and the minimal tooling required to make future auto-tune changes safer. The scope includes the advisor (recommendation engine) and the config rollout path (config-service + orchestrator), not model weights or operator changes.
postmortem_summary: What happened: the auto-tuner increased default batching factor and relaxed cache eviction thresholds in a canary that expanded to 40% of traffic. Unexpectedly, a subset of customer queries had heavy prefix churn causing larger KV cache memory usage and more offloads, which increased per-request token generation and caused queueing on constrained pods. Contributing factors: 1) no dry-run simulation against representative trace sets, 2) config rollout lacked a traffic quota circuit-breaker (only percentage-based canary), 3) insufficient preflight QPS/cost impact estimate, 4) observability dashboards did not surface token-level cost regressions quickly. Impact: short-term cost spike and elevated latency for 3 customers (medium severity).
root_causes: Auto-tuner defaulted to aggressive batching factor for small-traffic routes without per-route profile checks
KV cache eviction policy change increased memory residency and caused more cache thrashing for high-prefix-variance workloads
Config rollout did not support automatic revert based on economic alerts (only health/failure metrics were considered),
No representative dry-run/simulation harness to estimate token-cost and memory effects prior to rollout
mitigations: Introduce conservative initial multiplier for batching recommendations (max 1.25x) for first canary wave
Reinstate shorter default KV cache TTL for routes with high prefix churn and expose per-route override flag
Add token-budget alerts that trigger rollback when aggregate per-minute token spend on a deployment exceeds baseline + X%
Implement a preflight dry-run mode in the tuner that replays sampled traces and reports simulated cost/memory/latency deltas
Add automatic circuit-breaker to config rollout that can pause or revert expansion on economic alerts
Ship a migration script to add conservative settings to customers who received the aggressive config
playbook_steps: Preflight: run tuner dry-run on representative traces (use /tooling/trace-replay), capture token delta, memory delta, and request latency distribution
Start canary: apply change to 5% of traffic for 2h with 'conservative' multipliers; baseline metrics must be collected for 30m before expanding
Monitor: token_spend_per_min, tail_latency_p95/p99, cache_mem_rss, queue_length per pod and per-route; set economic_alert when spend > baseline * 1.12 over 10 minutes
Expansion gates: require economic_alert == false and error_rate <= baseline + 0.5% for 60m before doubling canary percentage
Automatic rollback: if economic_alert or latency gate trips, trigger config-service rollback to previous version and mark rollout as paused
Post-rollback triage: run targeted trace-replay to compare the rolled-back config and document differences; notify owners and affected customers
Approval: any expansion beyond 50% requires PM + SRE sign-off with documented cost/latency trade-offs
monitoring_alerts: economic_alert: alert if token_spend_aggregate_per_min > baseline * 1.12 for 10m
cache_mem_alert: per-node cache_memory_rss > 85% of node memory for 5m
queue_backpressure: request_queue_length > 10 for any serving pod for 2m
rollout_policy_proposal: Adopt a staged canary with conservative defaults: 5% -> 15% -> 40% -> 100% with minimum observation windows and both health and economic gates. Add 'dry-run' simulation step as mandatory for any change that touches batching or cache parameters. Expose a flag in the console 'Optimizetuner: safe_mode' that enforces conservative behavior for enterprise tenants by default.
